sources.title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval
sources.verified_evidence: Inspected the public arXiv HTML full text (v3, 2023-11-03), including abstract, method, and experiments. Section 3.1 generates item Semantic IDs by residual quantization of content embeddings; Section 3.2 trains a sequence-to-sequence model to predict the next item Semantic ID from a chronological user interaction sequence, with user-ID token personalization described in the experimental implementation. The abstract explicitly states prediction of the next item a user will interact with.

exact_overlap.user_next_item_behavior: Direct: predicts the next item from an individual user's ordered interaction history; user-specific tokens are additionally used for personalization.
exact_overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: No evidence found in inspected full text; semantic embeddings are quantized via RQ-VAE and no hyperbolic space/geometry is claimed.
exact_overlap.generative_semantic_ids: Direct: autoregressive generative retrieval predicts tuples of semantic codewords assigned to items.

sources.relevance: Strong evidence for the user-next-item plus generative-semantic-ID pair, but not the hyperbolic component.
limitations: Does not establish that hyperbolic geometry improves or is used in generative Semantic-ID next-item recommendation.
Experiments use three Amazon product-review categories; transfer to other domains/user behavior is not established by this citation.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Does representing item content and/or user histories in hyperbolic geometry improve personalized next-item prediction when the target is generated as a semantic ID?
behavior_problem_candidates.basis: TIGER independently verifies personalized sequential next-item generation with Semantic IDs, but the inspected full text does not study hyperbolic geometry. This is a research question/hypothesis, not an established finding.
behavior_problem_candidates.needed_evidence: A full-text paper explicitly combining hyperbolic representations or hyperbolic distance with autoregressive Semantic-ID prediction on user interaction sequences, or a controlled experiment testing that combination.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Can hyperbolic hierarchical structure help model user preference evolution or long-/short-term intent while generating the next Semantic ID?
behavior_problem_candidates.basis: TIGER reports hierarchical RQ-VAE codewords and sequence-based next-item prediction, but does not attribute the hierarchy to hyperbolic geometry or analyze preference evolution as a hyperbolic structure.
behavior_problem_candidates.needed_evidence: Full-text methods and results that define the user-behavior hierarchy, its hyperbolic embedding, and its effect on next-item outcomes.

limitations: The independently verified full text supports only two sides of the requested three-way intersection: user next-item behavior and generative Semantic IDs. No source in this result is verified to cover all three together.

FULL_TEXT means the linked arXiv HTML full text was inspected, not merely its abstract. The hyperbolic non-overlap statement is scoped to that inspected paper; it is not proof that no such paper exists.
Search integration attempts were unavailable, so this is not an exhaustive systematic review. Do not interpret absence of a verified intersection as evidence of nonexistence.
The arXiv DOI identifies the preprint record; the paper reports acceptance to NeurIPS 2023.
